profile_text.body:
Microsoft is a public company, traded as MSFT, founded in 1975 and headquartered in Redmond, Washington. Its most recent 10-K, covering the period ending 2026-06-30, reported revenue of $331,839,000,000. The page harvested from its site covers Power Automate, which the company describes as a way to automate workflows and business processes across apps, systems, and websites using AI, digital, and robotic process automation, and as able to automate across nearly unlimited systems, desktop apps, and websites. The site also presents a customer account stating that a data validation and standardization process that once took over 100 people can be managed by a few people with generative AI and Power Automate.

The company's tracked AI products span several areas. Microsoft Copilot is described as embedded across M365. Azure Machine Learning is listed as an MLOps platform with AutoML, a model registry, and responsible AI toolkit integration, and Azure OpenAI Service as offering OpenAI models in Azure regions with enterprise content filtering, Entra ID integration, and data residency controls. Developer tools include AutoGen, a multi-agent conversation framework, and Semantic Kernel, a model-agnostic orchestration SDK for .NET and Python that the material describes as superseded by Microsoft Agent Framework in 2026. Microsoft Agent Framework is listed as the successor to Semantic Kernel and AutoGen, a unified .NET and Python agent SDK with graph workflows and native MCP and A2A support. Other listed products are Microsoft Designer for image generation, Microsoft Teams AI for meeting recaps and intelligent recap, SharePoint AI for enterprise content, and Microsoft Clipchamp AI for video editing.

Two lawsuits are recorded against the company, both in the U.S. District Court, S.D. New York: The New York Times Co. v. Microsoft Corp. and OpenAI, and Authors Guild v. OpenAI, Inc.
